items.title: 6. Commercial TP-VAT on Repairs
items.text: Further to the above claim, I am contacting you regarding the claim we have been handling on behalf of our client, the repairs that were completed and the outstanding VAT element of £xxx owed to TBRN. When the incident was reported, we initially spoke with xxxxxx who confirmed that you were VAT registered and accordingly responsible for that element of the claim. Subject to the normal rules, a VAT registered company may treat any VAT incurred on the supply/repairs which can be recovered as input tax. The liability of the insurers is to ensure that you are not left at a financial loss, that means that they are liable to cover the reasonable cost so that you are not left out of pocket. When it comes to VAT, this can be recovered as part of your normal accounting procedures and so would not form part of your financial loss. As the works were carried out to your property/premises and you are the entity deriving benefit from the work completed, HMRC consider that you are able to reclaim the VAT on those repairs. The person responsible for causing the damage or for authorising the work is irrelevant for tax purposes in those circumstances. If it can be viewed a different way – had you obtained your own quotations for the work and proceeded with the same, our client would have reimbursed you the net amount only given that in the same way, you would be recovering the VAT that you had paid to your contractor. Please feel free to run this past your own accountants or consultants who will be able to confirm what we advise, I would therefore be grateful if you could arrange payment of the outstanding amount as soon as reasonably possible. If you have any queries then please do let me know.
